# B09 — Correctable memory and evidence-backed skill learning

[START](../../guide/00-START.md). Depends: B08. Outcome: a correction immediately changes subsequent behavior, and a learned skill improves held-out performance.

Read `server/memory/`, `server/learning/`, `server/conversations/`, `server/work/`. Load only functions for the active slice. Existing tests: `tests/memory/`, `tests/learning/`. New tests belong beside the behavior.

Planned files: `server/memory/corrections.ts`, `server/learning/skills.ts`, `server/learning/evaluation.ts`.

## Slices

- **s1:** Corrections. Resolve the specific fact/preference being corrected (ask if ambiguous). In one transaction: create a correction record linking old→new assertions, mark the old assertion `superseded` (retain history), store provenance, invalidate affected retrieval caches and derived skills, append an event. On the next turn retrieve the new assertion and exclude the superseded one. Test correction, supersession, cache invalidation, and persistence after closing and reopening the file database. J08 stands here.
- **s2:** Retrieval. Apply identity/lifecycle/sensitivity filters in the database first, then bounded lexical candidates plus optional qualified embedding candidates. Rank by relevance, recency and importance; preserve source IDs and correction links. Build a token-budgeted context with current instruction and relevant preferences first; do not silently slice off the user request. Summaries are lossy — fetch the original turn when exact wording matters. Evaluate on held-out Hinglish paraphrases. Test scoped retrieval, bounded paging, and paraphrase recall.
- **s3:** Skills. A skill is a versioned recipe: applicable conditions, tool schema versions, steps, evidence requirements and known failure cases. Candidate skills live separately from active skills. Observe completed jobs → propose one lesson → attach supporting/contradicting outcomes → evaluate on held-out cases in a sandbox → compare with baseline → promote only if the gate passes. Record skill version on every new job; roll back on regression. Never execute generated code merely because it was called a skill. Weight-training/fine-tuning is NOT part of this release. Test candidate→sandbox→promotion→rollback and that held-out metrics improve; transfer to unseen cases is measured, not assumed. J12 stands here.

Add numbered migrations only after inspecting the latest migration list; never rewrite applied SQL. Each slice must first exhibit the defect. Do not bundle all three into one small-model prompt.

## Gate

J08: after a correction and restart, the next response follows the corrected preference. J12: unseen wording and changed source documents still work via general logic, not fixture memorization. Skill promotion improves held-out metrics; regression triggers rollback. No weight training is performed.

Next: B10/s1. No new health probes here.
